mainTopic: The value of 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם,' רבי אביתר's ruling and reliability, and the danger of excessive fear at home
overview: The גמרא explains that even where a שליח does not have to say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם,' saying it helps. If the husband later challenges the גט, nobody listens to him. A ברייתא proves this: רבי ישמעאל told a man from כפר סיסאי to make the declaration, even though רבי אלעאי pointed out that the village counts as ארץ ישראל. Next, רבי אביתר rules that גיטין coming from בבל to ארץ ישראל need no declaration. The גמרא explains that so many people travel between the two lands that witnesses to confirm the גט are easy to find. רב יוסף doubts רבי אביתר's reliability, because he wrote a פסוק without lined parchment. אביי defends him: that rule is a tradition he may not have heard, and הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself quotes him in the story of the פילגש בגבעה. From that story, רב חסדא and רב warn against ruling a home with too much fear. רבה בר בר חנה then begins a comment on the three reminders said at home before שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'if you do it, you help' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the phrase 'if you do it, you help' from the earlier discussion and asks what benefit is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if you do it, you help.' What does 'if you do it, you help' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the discussion just before this. Someone was told he does not have to say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם,' but that saying it still helps. Now the גמרא asks what help that brings, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the declaration is not required, saying it seems pointless. The גמרא wants to know what real legal gain it gives.

phrases.english: And if you do it, you have helped.
phrases.notes: 'It' means saying 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' even when you don't have to.

phrases.english: What does 'if you do it, you have helped' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אִי עֲבַדְתְּ אַהְנֵית״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a phrase from the earlier discussion on the daf and asks for its meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concrete benefit comes from a voluntary declaration of בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם?

steps.title: The husband's challenge is ignored
steps.stepSummary: The benefit is that if the husband later comes to challenge the גט, we pay no attention to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband comes and challenges the גט, we do not pay attention to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the declaration protects the גט. If the husband later says it is not valid, בית דין ignores him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the declaration, a husband's challenge would force the woman to confirm the signatures with witnesses. With the שליח's declaration, the גט is already treated as confirmed, so the challenge has no force.

keyTerms.meaning: We pay no attention to him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם does more than meet a technical requirement. It also confirms the גט against later protests.

phrases.english: That if the husband comes and challenges it,
we pay no attention to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי אָתֵי בַּעַל מְעַרְעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The declaration makes the husband's later challenge irrelevant.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל tells the man from כפר סיסאי to make the declaration
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a man from כפר סיסאי who brought a גט to רבי ישמעאל. רבי ישמעאל told him to say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' so the woman would not need witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A man once brought a גט before רבי ישמעאל. He asked: Do I need to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' or not? רבי ישמעאל asked: My son, where are you from? He answered: רבי, I am from כפר סיסאי. רבי ישמעאל said: You need to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,' so that you won't need witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as proof that the declaration protects the גט. רבי ישמעאל told the שליח to say it so the woman would not later need witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'So that you won't need witnesses' means: if the husband protests, she will not have to bring witnesses to confirm the signatures. That is exactly the benefit described in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence

phrases.english: As it is taught: There was an incident with a certain man
who brought a גט before רבי ישמעאל.
He said to him: Do I need to say
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,'
or do I not need to?
He said to him: My son, where are you from?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, מִכְּפַר סִיסַאי אָנִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher, I am from the village of Sisai.
He said to him: You need to say
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,'
so that you won't need witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁהֵבִיא גֵּט לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the declaration protects the גט from the husband's later challenge.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל and the man from כפר סיסאי.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי objects that כפר סיסאי counts as ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי argues that כפר סיסאי sits inside ארץ ישראל and is closer than עכו. Even the רבנן agree such a place is like ארץ ישראל, so no declaration should be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the man left, רבי אלעאי came in before רבי ישמעאל and said: רבי, isn't כפר סיסאי surrounded by the borders of ארץ ישראל, and closer to ציפורי than עכו is? And we learned in a משנה: רבי מאיר says עכו is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין. Even the רבנן only argue with רבי מאיר about עכו, which is far. But about כפר סיסאי, which is close, they do not argue!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, רבי אלעאי challenges רבי ישמעאל's ruling. He argues that a גט from כפר סיסאי is a גט from ארץ ישראל, which needs no declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration is only required for a גט brought from outside ארץ ישראל. רבי אלעאי reasons: everyone agrees כפר סיסאי counts as ארץ ישראל, since it is closer than עכו and the רבנן only disagree about far-off עכו. So רבי ישמעאל seemingly asked for something unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Tzippori, a city in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעאי is not saying the גט is invalid. He is only questioning why the declaration was needed at all.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שֶׁיָּצָא, נִכְנַס לְפָנָיו רַבִּי אִלְעַאי,
phrases.english: After he left, רבי אלעאי came in before him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, וַהֲלֹא כְּפַר סִיסַאי
phrases.english: and said to him: My teacher, isn't the village of Sisai
enclosed within the border of ארץ ישראל,
and closer to Tzippori than Akko is?
And we learned: רבי מאיר says:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה at the start of גיטין, on 2a.

phrases.english: Akko is like ארץ ישראל for bills of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: And even the רבנן only disagree with רבי מאיר
about Akko, which is far away.
But the village of Sisai, which is close, no, they do not argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כְּפַר סִיסַאי מוּבְלַעַת בִּתְחוּם אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ישמעאל's ruling within the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's instruction to make the declaration for a גט from כפר סיסאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כפר סיסאי is agreed to be ארץ ישראל, and a גט from ארץ ישראל needs no declaration, so requiring it is unnecessary.

steps.title: Since it was done in a permitted way, it stands
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל tells רבי אלעאי to be quiet: since the divorce went out in a fully permitted way, it stands. This proves the declaration blocks the husband's challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Be quiet, my son, be quiet. Since the matter went out as permitted, it went out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers that the divorce is now done in a fully permitted way and stays that way. This closes the proof: the declaration made the גט secure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל agrees the declaration may not have been strictly needed. But because it was said, the גט was given in the most permitted way, with no room for the husband to challenge it. That is the meaning of 'if you do it, you help.'
steps.whatToRemember: Even where בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם is not required, saying it makes the גט fully secure. A husband who later protests is ignored.

phrases.english: He said to him: Be quiet, my son, be quiet.
Since the matter went out as permitted, it went out.
phrases.notes: He means the divorce now stands as fully valid, and nobody can take it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתוֹק בְּנִי, שְׁתוֹק, הוֹאִיל וְיָצָא הַדָּבָר בְּהֶיתֵּר – יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעאי's objection and completes the proof for step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that the declaration may not have been required, but defends it as having made the divorce fully secure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The declaration was pointless because כפר סיסאי is ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The declaration made the divorce go out fully permitted, so no later challenge can undo it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A voluntary declaration of בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם protects the גט, so a husband who later protests is ignored.

steps.title: Why did רבי אלעאי need to ask?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי ישמעאל already gave his reason ('so you will not need witnesses'), so why did רבי אלעאי question him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי ישמעאל also said to the man, 'so that you will not need witnesses'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי ישמעאל already explained his reason in the ברייתא. So why did רבי אלעאי object as if no reason had been given?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל told the man to make the declaration 'so the woman will not need witnesses.' That reason already shows the declaration protects the גט. So רבי אלעאי's objection seems to ignore something that was said right in front of him.

phrases.english: But he too
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי ישמעאל. He already gave his reason in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: 'so that you will not need witnesses'
he said to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיהוּ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the story itself: why was רבי אלעאי's objection, and רבי ישמעאל's answer, needed at all?
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעאי's objection in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל had already stated his reason, so רבי אלעאי should not have needed to ask.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי did not hear the full statement
steps.stepSummary: The people reporting the ruling to רבי אלעאי did not finish quoting it, so he never heard the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not finish telling it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעאי only heard part of רבי ישמעאל's words. The part with the reason never reached him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי's objection was fair based on what he knew. Since he did not hear 'so you will not need witnesses,' he thought the declaration was pointless in a place like כפר סיסאי.

keyTerms.meaning: before him, in front of him

phrases.english: They did not finish it before him.
phrases.notes: The people telling רבי אלעאי about the ruling stopped before the part with the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סַיְּימוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the reason was never reported to him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעאי heard the reason and still objected.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעאי only heard the ruling without its reason, so his question made sense.
steps.whatToRemember: The story stands as proof: the declaration of 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' helps by stopping the husband from later challenging the גט.

steps.title: רבי אביתר: גיטין from בבל need no declaration
steps.stepSummary: רבי אביתר wrote to רב חסדא that גיטין brought from בבל to ארץ ישראל do not need 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אביתר sent to רב חסדא: Bills of divorce that come from there (בבל) to here (ארץ ישראל) do not need the agent to say 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a letter from רבי אביתר. He rules that a גט brought from בבל to ארץ ישראל needs no declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גט brought from outside ארץ ישראל needs the declaration. רבי אביתר makes an exception for גיטין from בבל. The next steps will try to figure out why.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence'

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Evyatar sent to Rav Chisda:
Bills of divorce that come from there to here
phrases.notes: He is writing from ארץ ישראל, so 'there' is בבל and 'here' is ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: do not need one to say
'It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about where the declaration is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט brought from בבל to ארץ ישראל does not need the declaration.

steps.title: Is it because Babylonians know the law of לשמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי אביתר follows the reason that people are not experts in לשמה, and Babylonians are experts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say he holds that the reason is because people are not experts in writing for her sake, and these (Babylonians) are learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason behind רבי אביתר's ruling. Maybe the declaration exists because people don't know the rule of לשמה, and in בבל they do know it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of the מסכת (2b), רבה said the declaration exists because people outside ארץ ישראל are not experts in writing a גט לשמה. If Babylonians are experts, the declaration would not be needed there. This would make רבי אביתר's ruling fit רבה's reason only.

keyTerms.meaning: for her sake (written specifically for this woman)

phrases.english: Shall we say he holds
that it is because they are not experts in 'for her sake'
and these are learned?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the people of בבל, who know the laws well.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קָסָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the reason behind רבי אביתר's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אביתר's ruling depend on the reason of not being experts in לשמה?

steps.title: רבה also accepts רבא's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: even רבה agrees with רבא that the declaration is also needed to confirm the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? But רבה also holds the reason of רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. Even רבה agrees that the declaration is needed to confirm the גט, so knowing לשמה alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא said the declaration is needed to confirm the signatures (לקיימו). רבה holds that reason too, not only the לשמה reason. So even if Babylonians know לשמה, the need to confirm the גט remains, and the suggestion fails.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה and רבא. רבה gave the reason of לשמה; רבא gave the reason of confirming the גט. Here we learn that רבה accepts רבא's reason too.

phrases.english: And can you think so?!
But Rabba holds the view of Rava!
phrases.notes: רבא's reason, from the start of the מסכת, is that the declaration confirms the גט so no one can challenge the signatures.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרָא וְהָא רַבָּה אִית לֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reason of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי אביתר's ruling rests only on Babylonians knowing לשמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even רבה requires the declaration to confirm the גט, so knowing לשמה cannot remove the need.

steps.title: Witnesses are easy to find because many people travel
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the declaration is needed to confirm the גט, but between בבל and ארץ ישראל so many people travel that witnesses are easy to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees we need the declaration to confirm the גט. But since many people go up and come down, witnesses are commonly found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for רבי אביתר's ruling. Confirming the גט is still needed, but between בבל and ארץ ישראל it is easy to find witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the declaration is that it is hard to find witnesses from far away to confirm the signatures. Between בבל and ארץ ישראל, lots of people travel back and forth. So if the גט is challenged, witnesses who know the signatures can easily be found.

keyTerms.meaning: go up and come down (travel back and forth)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, רבי אביתר's ruling fits all opinions: the declaration is to confirm the גט, and between בבל and ארץ ישראל confirmation is easy because travelers are common.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
that we need it to confirm it
but since there are many
who go up and come down
they are commonly found.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בָּעֵינַן לְקַיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason of step 9 with a reason that fits everyone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that works for all opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אביתר's ruling depends on Babylonians knowing לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The declaration is for confirming the גט, and between בבל and ארץ ישראל witnesses are easy to find.

steps.title: רב יוסף doubts רבי אביתר's reliability
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks who says רבי אביתר is a reliable authority to rely on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Who will tell us that רבי אביתר is reliable?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the whole ruling by questioning whether רבי אביתר can be relied on. The next step brings his evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the ruling, רב יוסף attacks the source. If רבי אביתר is not reliable, his ruling does not need to be followed or explained.

keyTerms.meaning: someone reliable, an authority one can lean on

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Who will tell us
that Rabbi Evyatar is someone to rely on?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּרַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר בַּר סַמְכָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of explaining רבי אביתר's ruling, questions whether he can be relied on at all.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The authority of רבי אביתר's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His reliability as a source is in doubt.

steps.title: רב יוסף's evidence: רבי אביתר's letter to רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אביתר wrote to רב יהודה that Babylonians who move to ארץ ישראל fulfill a harsh פסוק, and he wrote the פסוק without lined parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, he is the one who sent to רב יהודה: People who go up from there to here fulfill in themselves 'And they gave a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, and drank.' And he wrote it to him without lines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings proof for his doubt: in a letter to רב יהודה, רבי אביתר wrote a פסוק without scored lines. This sets up the rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harsh words about people from בבל are only the content of the letter. The evidence רב יוסף relies on is that רבי אביתר wrote a פסוק on parchment without lines. The next step brings the rule that shows this was a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: those who go up (move to ארץ ישראל)
scored lines on parchment for writing

phrases.english: And furthermore, he is the one
who sent to Rav Yehuda:
People who go up from there to here
have fulfilled in themselves:
'And they have given a boy for a prostitute,
phrases.notes: יואל 4:3. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: and sold a girl for wine, and have drunk.'
phrases.notes: He means these people leave their families behind when they move.

phrases.english: And he wrote it to him without scored lines;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד הָא אִיהוּ דִּשְׁלַח לֵיהּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's doubt from step 12 with evidence.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי אביתר is not reliable
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אביתר's letter to רב יהודה, in which he wrote a פסוק without שירטוט

steps.title: The rule that shows רבי אביתר made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings the rule of רבי יצחק and a ברייתא that limit how many words of a פסוק may be written without lined parchment, showing that רבי אביתר broke it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: two words may be written without lines, but three may not. A ברייתא teaches: three may be written, but four may not!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף completes his attack. He brings the rule about writing פסוקים without lines, to show that רבי אביתר did something wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רבי אביתר wrote a whole פסוק without lining the parchment. Here רב יוסף shows the rule: only two words (or three, according to the ברייתא) may be written that way. If רבי אביתר did not know this rule, רב יוסף argues, why should we rely on him?

keyTerms.meaning: Scoring lines into the parchment so the writing comes out straight
Two words may be written without lines
A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

steps.confusionAlert: There are two versions of the rule here (two words or three words). Both versions agree that a full פסוק needs lines. That is the whole point of the attack.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Two [words] one may write [without lines],
three one may not write;
in a ברייתא it was taught:
three one may write, four one may not write!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שְׁתַּיִם כּוֹתְבִין, שָׁלֹשׁ אֵין כּוֹתְבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the rule that turns step 13's story into a challenge against רבי אביתר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliability of רבי אביתר as an authority, and so his ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He wrote a full פסוק without lines, against a known rule. So he does not seem to be a reliable authority.

steps.title: Not knowing a tradition does not make someone less of a scholar
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a scholar can only be faulted for missing something that logic shows. This rule is a received tradition, and רבי אביתר may simply never have heard it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is everyone who does not know this rule of רבי יצחק not a great man?! If it were a matter of reasoning, fine. But this is a received tradition, and he never heard it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף's attack and defends רבי אביתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי splits mistakes into two kinds. Missing something you could figure out with logic (סברא) would show weakness. Missing a tradition passed down from teachers (גמרא) only shows that you never heard it. The שרטוט rule is the second kind, so רבי אביתר's greatness stays intact.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, a reliable scholar
Here: a received tradition passed down from teachers

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition learned from a teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: The split between סברא and גמרא shows how the גמרא judges a scholar: by his reasoning, not by whether he heard every tradition.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is that to say that anyone who does not know
this ruling of Rabbi Yitzchak
is not a great man?!
Granted, a matter that depends on reasoning — fine;
phrases.notes: He means: if he had missed something logical, then you could fault him.

phrases.english: but this is a received tradition,
and he did not hear the tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ כֹּל דְּלָא יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection רב יוסף raised in steps 12-14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the שרטוט mistake makes רבי אביתר unreliable.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The attack treats not knowing a received tradition as if it were a failure of reasoning.

steps.title: רבי אביתר's opinion on the פילגש בגבעה
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second defense: הקדוש ברוך הוא agreed with רבי אביתר. He first brings the dispute between רבי אביתר and רבי יונתן about why the husband got angry at the פילגש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, this is רבי אביתר, whose Master agreed with him. As it is written: "And his concubine strayed from him." רבי אביתר says: he found a fly. רבי יונתן says: he found a hair.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a second, stronger proof that רבי אביתר is great. He first sets up the dispute that the story in the next step will be about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the פילגש left her husband, and the חכמים ask what made him so angry. רבי אביתר says he found a fly (in his food), and רבי יונתן says he found a hair. This dispute is the background for the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His Master (הקדוש ברוך הוא) agreed with him

phrases.english: And furthermore, this is Rabbi Evyatar
whose Master agreed with him;
as it is written: "And his concubine strayed from him,"

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר אָמַר: זְבוּב מָצָא לָהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Evyatar says: He found a fly [by her].
phrases.notes: He means a fly in the food she made for him, which made him angry.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן אָמַר: נִימָא מָצָא לָהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says: He found a hair [by her].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא רַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר הוּא דְּאַסְכֵּים מָרֵיהּ עַל יְדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second defense of רבי אביתר on top of אביי's first answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אביתר is a great and reliable scholar.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute about the פילגש בגבעה, which sets up the story of אליהו.

steps.title: אליהו reports that הקדוש ברוך הוא quotes רבי אביתר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אביתר meets אליהו, who tells him that הקדוש ברוך הוא is learning about the פילגש בגבעה and quoting the opinions of both רבי אביתר and רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אביתר met אליהו and asked: What is הקדוש ברוך הוא doing? He answered: He is learning about the פילגש בגבעה. And what is He saying? He answered: "אביתר My son says this, יונתן My son says this."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that proves its point: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself quotes רבי אביתר's opinion by name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו's report shows that רבי אביתר's teaching is repeated in Heaven and that he is called "My son." Someone whose words הקדוש ברוך הוא quotes is clearly a great scholar. So רב יוסף's doubt from the שרטוט mistake falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who sometimes appeared to the חכמים
The story of the concubine in Givah (שופטים chapters 19-21)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף doubted רבי אביתר because of a שרטוט mistake. אביי answers that missing a tradition is no flaw, and that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself quotes רבי אביתר as "My son."

phrases.english: And Rabbi Evyatar found Eliyahu,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי קָא עָבֵיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא?
phrases.english: he said to him: What is the Holy One, Blessed be He, doing?
He said to him: He is busy with the concubine in Givah.
And what is He saying? He said to him:
"Evyatar, My son, says this,
Yonatan, My son, says this."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר לְאֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof begun in step 16 by showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא quotes רבי אביתר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אביתר is a great authority whose words can be relied on.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אליהו's report that הקדוש ברוך הוא quotes "אביתר My son."

steps.title: Can Heaven Be Unsure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אביתר is shocked that הקדוש ברוך הוא would quote two different opinions, as if He were in doubt about what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אביתר said to אליהו: God forbid! Can there be any doubt before Heaven?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אביתר reacts to what אליהו told him in the last step. He asks how הקדוש ברוך הוא could quote two opinions, as if He did not know which one was true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting two opinions sounds like being unsure about which one is right. But Heaven knows everything, so quoting both seems impossible. This question sets up אליהו's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: before Heaven, meaning before הקדוש ברוך הוא

phrases.english: He said to him: God forbid!
phrases.notes: This is רבי אביתר talking to אליהו.

phrases.english: Is there any doubt before Heaven?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא סְפֵיקָא קַמֵּי שְׁמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how הקדוש ברוך הוא could quote two opinions, which אליהו reported in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that הקדוש ברוך הוא quotes both רבי אביתר and רבי יונתן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Quoting two possible opinions suggests doubt, and there can be no doubt before Heaven.

steps.title: Both Opinions Are True: A Fly, Then a Hair
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that both opinions are the words of the living God, because both things really happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to him: These and those are both the words of the living God. He found a fly and was not bothered; he found a hair and was bothered.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers that there is no doubt in Heaven. Both opinions are true because both events happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions do not argue about the facts. Each one names a different event that really took place. First the husband found a fly and let it go. Later he found a hair, and that is what made him angry.

keyTerms.meaning: these and those are the words of the living God
he became upset; he took it seriously

steps.whatToRemember: There is no doubt in Heaven. Both רבי אביתר and רבי יונתן described something that really happened: the fly came first and was ignored, and the hair came next and caused the anger.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the famous phrase אלו ואלו דברי אלהים חיים means both facts actually happened. It does not mean two opposite rulings are both correct.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes אביי's second defense of רבי אביתר from step 16. Heaven itself quotes רבי אביתר, which shows he is a great authority.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים הֵן –
phrases.english: These and those are the words of the living God:
he found a fly and was not bothered,
he found a hair and was bothered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אביתר's question from step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both opinions are combined as two events that each really happened
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Quoting two opinions would mean Heaven is unsure
steps.terutzMaskana: Both happened, one after the other: the fly was ignored and the hair caused the anger

steps.title: Where the Fly and Hair Were Found: רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the fly was in the dish and the hair was on her body. The fly was only disgusting, but the hair was dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The fly was in the dish, and the hair was in 'that place.' A fly is just disgusting, but a hair there is a danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains why the husband ignored the fly but got angry about the hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two findings were in different places and had different weight. A fly in food is only unpleasant. A hair in an intimate place could cause physical harm, so it was more serious and led to his anger.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said: The fly was in the dish,
and the hair was in 'that place';
The fly was only disgusting, but the hair was dangerous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: זְבוּב בַּקְּעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the fly and hair mentioned in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fly was in the food and was merely disgusting; the hair was on her body and was dangerous, so only the hair angered him.

steps.title: Second Version: Both Were in the Dish
steps.stepSummary: Another version says both the fly and the hair were in the dish. The fly was not her fault, but the hair came from her carelessness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Both were in the dish. The fly was out of her control, but the hair was her negligence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the difference between the fly and the hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version both were found in the food, so the difference is not about place. A fly can fall in by itself, so she could not prevent it. A hair in the food comes from not being careful, so he blamed her for it.

keyTerms.meaning: this one and that one; both

phrases.english: Some say: Both this and that were in the dish;
the fly was beyond her control, but the hair was negligence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בַּקְּעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation from רב יהודה's in step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both were in the food; the fly was unavoidable, while the hair showed carelessness.

steps.title: Never Impose Too Much Fear at Home
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a person should never put excessive fear on his household, learning this from the פילגש בגבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A person should never put too much fear on his household. The husband of the פילגש בגבעה put too much fear on her, and it caused the deaths of many tens of thousands of Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from explaining the story to drawing a life lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's harsh anger made his פילגש so afraid that she ran away. The events that followed ended in a terrible war. רב חסדא learns from this that creating too much fear at home can lead to disaster.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a story from the Bible into practical guidance for how a person should run his home.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
A person should never impose
excessive fear within his home,
for look at the פילגש בגבעה:
her husband imposed excessive fear on her,
and it brought down many tens of thousands of Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַל יָטִיל אָדָם אֵימָה יְתֵירָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a moral lesson from the פילגש בגבעה story discussed in steps 16–21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must never impose excessive fear on his household.

steps.title: Too Much Fear Leads to Three Sins
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that one who imposes excessive fear at home will end up with three severe sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who puts too much fear on his household will end up coming to three sins: forbidden relations, bloodshed, and desecrating שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching adds to רב חסדא's warning. It lists three serious sins that result from a home ruled by fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא names the sins but does not explain how each one happens. The common idea is that a frightened family member may hide the truth or act out of panic. For example, she might say she went to the מקוה when she did not, run away into danger, or cook on שבת out of fear of his anger.
steps.whatToRemember: Too much fear at home is not just unpleasant. רב חסדא shows it can cause a disaster, and רב says it leads to גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, and חילול שבת.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמֵּטִיל אֵימָה יְתֵירָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who imposes excessive fear within his home

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף הוּא בָּא לִידֵי שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת:
phrases.english: will in the end come to three sins:

phrases.aramaic: גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, וְחִילּוּל שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: forbidden relations, bloodshed, and desecrating שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמֵּטִיל אֵימָה יְתֵירָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב חסדא's warning by listing three sins that come from excessive fear
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Imposing excessive fear at home leads to גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, and חילול שבת.

steps.title: Three things to say at home before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes the rule of the חכמים that before שבת a person must ask his household whether they separated מעשרות and made the עירוב, and must tell them to light the candles. He then begins to add his own requirement about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: about this rule of the Rabbis, that a person must say three things in his home on Friday as it gets dark ('Did you tithe? Did you make the עירוב? Light the candle!'), he must... (his point continues in the next lines).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה quotes a famous rule about three reminders a person gives his family right before שבת. He is setting up his own comment on that rule, which begins with 'צריך' and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted rule lists two questions that check for jobs that cannot be done once שבת begins: separating מעשרות and making an עירוב. The third line, lighting the candle, is an instruction. The גמרא here does not explain why this line is an instruction or why it comes last. Since the גמרא was just discussing not ruling a home with fear, רבה בר בר חנה's point will be about how these reminders should be said.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is getting dark, close to nightfall
Have you separated מעשרות (tithes) from the food?
Have you made the עירוב, the arrangement that allows carrying on שבת?
Light the candle, meaning the שבת lamp

steps.confusionAlert: The last word, צריך ('he must'), does not belong to the rule of the רבנן. It is the start of רבה בר בר חנה's own addition, which finishes at the top of the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
This that the Rabbis said:
Three things a person must say

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם חֲשֵׁיכָה:
phrases.english: in his home on Shabbat eve as it gets dark:
Have you tithed? Have you made the eiruv?
Light the lamp!
He must...
phrases.notes: This is רבה בר בר חנה starting his own point. His sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הָא דְּאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of how a man should behave toward his household, moving from warnings against excessive fear to a practical ערב שבת routine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before שבת, a person must remind his household about מעשרות and the עירוב and tell them to light the candles. רבה בר בר חנה begins to add a requirement about this, which continues in the next lines.
